newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Res surges on red-chips demand.
newsitem.headline: China Res surges on red-chips demand.

text.p: Shares of China Resources Enterprise Ltd surged on rotational demand for red-chips on Tuesday, particularly ahead of the company's earnings report due next week, brokers said.
"Rotational buying for leading red-chips, especially listed vehicles backed by Chinese authorities, fueled demand for the stock," said a dealing director at a regional brokerage.
China Resources shares rose HK$1.30 to HK$19.70 at midday on volume of 10.58 million shares.
The company is ultimately controlled by China's Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Co-operation.

Brokers said investors were seen accumulating the stock ahead of the release of its final results due next Monday and on expectation of good profit from its upcoming sales at its Nga Ying Chau residential complex on Tsing Yi in Hong Kong.
The Nga Ying Chau development is a joint venture in which China Resources holds a 55 percent interest while Cheung Kong Holdings Ltd and Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd each holds a 22.5 percent stake.
